reason: Both tanks need filling, and the methane store matches the lander's methane tank.
expectation: I expect methane to transfer into its flight tank; I don't know whether that alone will complete part of the goal.

alternatives.reason: The oxygen tank also needs filling, but either matching transfer seems like a reasonable place to start.

effect: The methane tank is filled through its dedicated line, leaving the oxygen tank to fill.
reaction: The separate connection makes the transfer straightforward, though the result was expected.
reason: The oxygen store matches the remaining flight tank and is the only numbered action offered.
expectation: I expect liquid oxygen to transfer into its separate tank and complete the filling goal.

effect: The oxygen transfer filled the second tank and completed the chapter. The result clarified that fuel and oxidizer remain separate until they meet in the engine.
reaction: The explanation of where the two liquids meet was a useful detail in an otherwise predictable transfer.

mostWorthwhile.text: Filling the oxygen tank was most worthwhile because its result explained why the two liquids have separate tanks and where they meet.

leastWorthwhile.text: Filling the methane tank was straightforward but offered little decision-making beyond matching the store to the tank.

surprise.text: The engine detail sharpened my understanding of how the separate supplies are used, though the transfer itself was expected.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary; both matched a named liquid store to its corresponding flight tank.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the return and the specimens' examination unfold, though this chapter's two obvious transfers offered little gameplay challenge.
